text:
alex: FYI my YAML tried to unionize overnight. It added a `go-slow: true` key and refused to parse until treated with coffee. :coffee:
mina: lol mine edited the changelog to: 'minor feelings only, no breaking promises.'
rohan: Can we start using emotional semver? Major when you ghost the team, minor when you bring snacks, patch when you fix a typo.
ci-bot: Build report: changelog-empathy.md added. Lint status: feelings-ok, indentation-ambiguous at lines 3-5.
tess: someone on the 3rd floor stuck a sticker: "I survived merge conflicts and all I got was this YAML." :stuck_out_tongue:
alex: quick poll: which causes more guilt in production? a) semver fibs like `v2.0-maybe` b) YAML with two spaces then a tab c) commit message that starts with 'wip but ship'
mina: :one: for semver fibs. They lie to product managers.
rohan: :two: tabs will make the parser cry silently for days.
tess: :three: is my life's brand.
ci-bot: Note: avoid tags like `v1.0-ish` per release policy. Automated rollback enabled for ambiguous tags.
mina: new meme: when you open a config and see `version: latest` and immediately call HR.
rohan: Favorite recent commit title: "fix: coax YAML into adulthood" with diff:
```diff
- tabs: \n+ tabs: no thanks
- version: 1.2.3
+ version: 1.2.3-therapy
```
alex: also heard at lunch: the compiler started a podcast called "Borrow Check & Chill." Guests: GCC and a patched linter.
tess: This thread summary: coffee, therapy for config, and an ultimatum to semver. :coffee: :heart:
ci-bot: Reminder: please run `make lint-yaml` before merging. It has feelings, too.
mina: Closing with sticker idea: 'YAML: where whitespace goes to find itself' :sparkles:
